facts.statement: Sierritasuchus is known from a small holotype skeleton found in the Late Triassic Tecovas Formation of Texas.
facts.quote: It is known from a small holotype skeleton from the Late Triassic Tecovas Formation of Texas.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton, cataloged as UMMP V60817, was discovered in 1939 and was originally classified as Desmatosuchus.
facts.quote: This skeleton (known as UMMP V60817) was discovered in 1939 and was originally assigned to the genus Desmatosuchus.

facts.statement: The species was moved to its own genus in 2008, with the type species designated as S. macalpini.
facts.quote: It was placed in its own genus in 2008 after having been in the collections of the University of Michigan Museum of Paleontology, with the type species being S. macalpini.

facts.statement: The genus name honors the location Sierrita de la Cruz Creek, while the species name honors the discoverer Archie MacAlpin.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to Sierrita de la Cruz Creek where the holotype was found, and the specific name refers to Archie MacAlpin, who discovered the skeleton.

facts.statement: Histological analysis of the scutes indicates the holotype individual was a subadult that had not reached full maturity.
facts.quote: Based on the histology of the scutes of the holotype, the individual was a subadult that was not fully grown.

facts.statement: Sierritasuchus is distinguished by recurved spines along its sides that feature serrations on their front edges.
facts.quote: Unlike other aetosaurs, Sierritasuchus has recurved spines along its side that are serrated on the front edges.

facts.statement: In Sierritasuchus, the dorsal eminence extends to touch the posterior margin of the paramedian scute.
facts.quote: In Sierritasuchus, the dorsal eminence touches the posterior margin of the paramedian scute.

facts.statement: Both the paramedian and lateral scutes of Sierritasuchus possess anterior bars.
facts.quote: Both the paramedian and lateral scutes (which run along the side of the animal beneath the paramedians) have anterior bars.

facts.statement: Sierritasuchus is classified as an extinct genus of aetosaur belonging to the subfamily Desmatosuchinae.
facts.quote: Sierritasuchus is an extinct genus of aetosaur in the subfamily Desmatosuchinae.

facts.statement: The parent group of Sierritasuchus is the tribe Desmatosuchini.
Sierritasuchus belongs to the family Stagonolepididae.
Sierritasuchus lived during the Late Triassic period.
The time range for Sierritasuchus spans from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Additionally, there is a distinct ridge on the posterior surface of each dorsal eminence.
